event: The high-score table scrolls up as the song loads: AWN, 942,110, third, four months old.

memory.fact: A rhythm cabinet at Full Combo shows a 942k score Aura has not cleared.

event: It's Awen's tag, from the night she took this cabinet off Aura and kept it.
What holds her is the company: every other row on the board is one of Aura's tags.
Aura wipes strangers' records like straightening a picture, yet has left this one.
Awen says nothing and files it with the carried thing and the covered sentence.
Aura drops onto the pad beside her, shoulder to shoulder, thumbing the difficulty up.
"Stop dating the machine. Date me." Awen says she's studying the competition.
"You're third." "I'm studying how you'll feel in a minute about being second."
The song hits and the talking stops; arrows come faster than banter.
Four feet thud on two pads; the screen light goes frantic on both their faces.
Aura is better, as always, but Awen keeps up beside her.
Their elbows knock on the crossovers and neither fixes her spacing.
The last note lands; Aura won it, and neither of them looks at the screen.
Both breathe hard; Aura's ponytail has lost its argument with the evening.
Aura looks at Awen instead of the board she just topped.
"Okay," Awen says, smaller than she meant, and reaches into her bag.
The tired tape gives without a sound; she holds the thing out flat in the blue light.
It's a brass key, its blade cut by hand on the mill at her shop to one particular lock.

memory.fact: Awen made Aura a brass shop-key: a wind-rose bow fused to a hand-cut blade.

event: Its bow is an openwork wind rose, enamelled the deep blue the cabinets throw in the dark.
The blue took her three tries to lie down flat; she got it on the third.
She doesn't say what it opens; she wants to see if Aura gets there herself.
Aura takes it and, for once, doesn't fill the silence.
Her thumb finds the wind rose and stays; Awen thinks everyone likes the pretty part.
Then Aura turns it and runs her thumb along the blade's cuts, and the fast leaves her face.
"This is your shop," she says slowly. "You made me a key to your shop."
Awen: front and back, same key; the back door sticks, you lift while you turn.

memory.fact: The shop-key is cut alike to the shop's own key.

event: She stops mid-excuse; she likes that door exactly that stubborn anyway.
Aura has closed her fist round the key, the wind rose vanished, gone still on both feet.
Aura: she holds every record in the place, and this is number one now.
She won't stand it on a shelf.
She threads it onto the carabiner at her hip: arcade, back room, roll-gate out front.

memory.fact: Aura keeps her everyday keys on a carabiner.

event: Brass rings once against steel as the ring drops back against her hip.

memory.fact: The shop-key hangs on Aura's everyday carabiner.

event: "Okay. Put the bag down." Awen puts the bag down.
Aura kisses her, or she kisses Aura; they have never settled who starts it.
They are miles past first kisses, but a cold edge of brass is caught at the hip.
Aura kisses her like there's no queue behind it and nowhere after this to be.
Awen's hand finds the back of Aura's neck and pulls her in past her carefulness.
The key digs in between them and neither moves it.
Aura makes a sound into her mouth that isn't a word; Awen swallows it and gives one back.
Aura kisses all-in now, the slow gone, the fast back but aimed.
Both her hands go up into Awen's hair, working the pin loose.
The whole dark weight of Awen's hair comes down.
She laughs against Awen's mouth, the pin shut in her fist like she won it.
"That was a good pin," Awen says.
"I'll build you a better one": a lie, since she couldn't build a sandwich, and both know it.
She walks Awen backward past the dark cabinets toward the stairs at the back.
The bag stays on the floor; the key is cold at her hip.
"I'll build you a whole—"
Awen kisses her quiet before she has to finish lying about it.
They go up.
